spotters.exp: Father of modern plastic surgery. Pioneered tube pedicle flaps and facial reconstruction of WWI soldiers
American otolaryngologist; performed the first documented endonasal (closed) rhinoplasty in 1887. Pioneer of aesthetic facial surgery and early nasal tip modification
Father of laser medicine and surgery. First to apply laser beams (ruby and CO2) to human skin in the early 1960s
Monumental 19th-century German dermatologist. Described nevus sebaceus of Jadassohn and Jadassohn-Lewandowsky syndrome
German surgeon; eponym of the Burow's triangle used in dog-ear and advancement flap repair. Also lends his name to Burow's solution (aluminium acetate astringent)
Described the donor dominance principle (1959) — transplanted follicles retain DHT-resistance regardless of recipient site. Father of modern hair transplantation; also pioneered subcision for scars
Turkish physician (1897). Eponym of Hodara disease — trichoclasis-type hair breakage he described
Japanese physician credited with an early follicular punch hair transplantation technique (1930s). Restored hair in scarred/burned scalp decades before Orentreich
Pioneering Indian dermatologist, a founding figure of organised dermatology in India. Note: a second portrait (e5aad83c-23dc-403f-ae1b-ff4e4816818a.jpeg) also appears in the source
One of the inventors of the laser; coined the acronym LASER. Won a long-running patent battle for key laser patents
Indian-American physicist who invented the CO2 laser (1964). The CO2 laser is a workhorse for ablative resurfacing and cutaneous surgery
Built the first working laser — a ruby laser — in 1960. Ruby laser later used for tattoo and pigment removal
Developed Intense Pulsed Light (IPL) technology. IPL is a broadband (non-laser) source for pigment, vascular lesions and photorejuvenation

spotters.q: Identify the clinical sign / pathological finding shown:
spotters.exp: Eosinophilic intranuclear pseudoinclusions in atypical plasma cells. Not true nuclear inclusions — invaginations of immunoglobulin-rich cytoplasm into the nucleus

spotters.q: Identify the clinical sign / pathological finding shown:
spotters.exp: Linear depression along the course of superficial veins when the limb is elevated. Classic sign of eosinophilic fasciitis (Shulman syndrome)

spotters.q: Identify the clinical sign / pathological finding shown:
spotters.exp: PTEN hamartoma tumor syndrome (PTEN mutation). Triad: macrocephaly, intestinal hamartomatous polyps, and pigmented penile macules

spotters.q: Identify the clinical sign / pathological finding shown:
spotters.exp: Violaceous (lilac) periorbital erythema with eyelid edema. Pathognomonic cutaneous sign of dermatomyositis

spotters.q: Identify the clinical sign / pathological finding shown:
spotters.exp: Urbach-Wiethe disease — autosomal recessive, ECM1 gene mutation. Hoarse cry from infancy, beaded eyelid papules (moniliform blepharosis), waxy skin infiltration

spotters.q: Identify the clinical sign / pathological finding shown:
spotters.exp: Eponymous clinical spotter (labelled Nazaroo in the source). Identify by the depicted morphology

spotters.q: Identify the clinical sign / pathological finding shown:
spotters.exp: Linear, cord-like rope-like indurated band, typically on the trunk/flanks. Associated with interstitial granulomatous dermatitis (seen in Ackerman syndrome)

spotters.q: Identify the clinical sign / pathological finding shown:
spotters.exp: Hair shaft showing a club / mace-shaped swollen tip. A trichoscopic spotter of abnormal hair-shaft morphology

spotters.q: Identify the clinical sign / pathological finding shown:
spotters.exp: Segmental narrowing of the hair shaft (a Beau's-line equivalent for hair). Reflects a transient matrix insult — chemotherapy, severe illness, or stress

spotters.q: Identify the anatomical line or landmark shown:
spotters.exp: Down-turned furrows from the labial commissures to the lateral chin. Caused by mandibular bone resorption, fat-pad atrophy, and pull of the depressor anguli oris (DAO)

spotters.q: Identify the anatomical line or landmark shown:
spotters.exp: The Frankfort horizontal plane — from the infraorbital rim to the superior margin of the external auditory meatus (porion). Standard reference plane for cephalometry and aesthetic facial analysis

spotters.q: Identify the anatomical line or landmark shown:
spotters.exp: Reference lines used to locate the ideal malar (cheekbone) prominence. Their intersection marks the point of maximal malar projection for augmentation

spotters.q: Identify the anatomical line or landmark shown:
spotters.exp: Facial fat is compartmentalized into discrete superficial and deep fat pads. Includes malar (medial/middle/lateral), nasolabial, and deep medial cheek compartments
Spotter retained as labelled in the source (spelling uncertain). Identify by the depicted image
Topical minoxidil, brand name Rogaine. Vasodilator that prolongs the anagen phase; first-line for androgenetic alopecia
Complementary-colour correction chart for camouflage make-up. Green neutralises red (erythema/telangiectasia); orange/peach neutralises blue-brown dyschromia
Green bottle fly — larvae used for maggot debridement therapy (MDT). Sterile larvae selectively digest necrotic tissue; ~1000 maggots applied for 1-3 days
